## MEET THE CREATIVE TEAM
#### ANNABELLE LOPEZ OCHOA
![](https://www.ballethispanico.org/uploads/FY26%20Season/ALO_Headshot4x5_March2026.png)
#### Choreography
Annabelle Lopez Ochoa is a Belgian-Colombian choreographer whose work has reshaped contemporary ballet on the global stage. Trained at the Royal Ballet School in Antwerp, she began her professional life as a dancer, performing for twelve years with leading European companies including Djazzex and Scapino Ballet Rotterdam. In 2003, she made the pivotal decision to devote herself fully to choreography, and almost immediately was hailed as a “rising star” of the Dutch dance scene.
Since then, Lopez Ochoa has become one of the most prolific and sought-after choreographic voices, with original works created for well over companies across Europe, the Americas, Asia, and Australia. Her roster includes commissions for New York City Ballet, San Francisco Ballet, English National Ballet, Dutch National Ballet, Hong Kong Ballet, Queensland Ballet, Atlanta Ballet, Scottish Ballet, Ballet Nacional de Cuba, Pacific Northwest Ballet, and — among many others — Ballet Hispánico New York.
Lopez Ochoa’s work spans an extraordinary breadth of forms: short conceptual pieces, full-length narrative ballets, theatrical works, opera, musical theatre, and dance films. She is widely respected for her ability to weave emotional depth with architectural clarity, crafting movement that is richly detailed yet structurally dynamic.
#### CHRISTOPHER ASH
![](https://www.ballethispanico.org/uploads/FY27%20Season/Creative%20Team/DonQ_CAsh.png)
#### Scenic and Lighting Design
Christopher’s dance credits include Ballet Hispánico, BalletX, Northern Ballet, Arizona Ballet, Miami City Ballet, Houston Ballet, Municipal de Santiago, Atlanta Ballet, Hubbard Street 2, and River North Chicago Dance.  
  
Broadway credits include _New York, New York_ , _Sunday in the Park with George_ , and _Saint Joan_. Opera credits include The Metropolitan Opera, Paris Opera, La Monnaie, Lausanne, Lyric Opera of Chicago, Canadian Opera, and Houston Grand Opera. Regional theater work includes the Guthrie Theater, Wilma Theater, Philadelphia Theatre Company, and Yale Repertory Theatre. His work has been seen in 19 countries and recognized with 17 awards. Christopher holds an MFA from the Yale School of Drama.
#### JUAN PABLO ACOSTA
![](https://www.ballethispanico.org/uploads/FY27%20Season/Creative%20Team/DonQ_JP%20Acosta.png)
#### Music Arranger and Composer
Musical director, composer, arranger, producer, and performer. Holds a Bachelor of Music degree with a focus on classical guitar, and a Master’s degree in Latin and Caribbean Music from the University of Antioquia, graduating cum laude for his distinguished research work.  
  
Nominated for a Latin Grammy Award in 2025 and 2025 with Los Cumbia Stars, and for over 20 years has served as musical director and composer for Colombia’s most renowned dance company, Ballet Folclórico de Antioquia (BFDA), participating in over 600 local and national performances, and more than 200 international shows across 18 countries.  
  
As a composer, he has written six major ballets for prestigious institutions such as Miami City Ballet (USA), Houston Ballet (USA), Alberta Ballet (Canada), Cincinnati Ballet (USA), Ballet Nacional Dominicano, Ballet Folklórico de Antioquia, and Ballet Metropolitano de Medellín.
#### TITUS TIEL GROENESTEGE
![](https://www.ballethispanico.org/uploads/FY27%20Season/Creative%20Team/DonQ_Titus.png)
#### Dramaturgy
Titus Tiel Groenestege (1959, The Netherlands) finished Utrecht Theatre School in 1981 and in the same year won a comedy festival with his stage partner Bavo Galama. 'Something in between drama and comedy' the newspapers wrote.  
  
In 1984 Titus played the title role in Shakespeare's Hamlet. In 1990 he became a duo with Han Römer and they made several semi-philosophical shows. In 1998 he started working with Ria Marks under the umbrella of Orkater (Orchestra & Theatre) They created highly acclaimed and successful productions without dialogue that were played all over the world.  
  
Although still active as an actor, the last 25 years Titus has mainly been known as a director. His field of work covers theatre, cabaret, slapstick, music theatre, bands, classical orchestras, dance and physical theatre
#### MARK ZAPPONE
![](https://www.ballethispanico.org/uploads/FY27%20Season/Creative%20Team/DonQ_Mark.png)
#### Costume Design
Mark A. Zappone served Pacific Northwest Ballet (PNB) for five seasons as costume designer, shop supervisor, and wardrobe master (1983-1988). He then moved to Monte Carlo, where he managed costume shops for Les Ballets de Monte-Carlo and Le Cabaret de Monte-Carlo, and subsequently continued on to Switzerland and Amsterdam with Holiday on Ice, and then back to Seattle to work with a variety of companies, including PNB. Zappone has collaborated with many well-known choreographers and designers, including Lucinda Childs, Maurice Sendak, Christopher Wheeldon, Kent Stowell, Jerome Kaplan, Twyla Tharp, Price Suddarth, George Balanchine Trust, Helgi Tomasson, Molissa Fenley, Mark Morris Annabelle Lopez Ochoa , Martin Pakledinez, Christopher Stowell, Yuri Possokhov, Paul Tazewell, Matthew Neenan and Nuno Corte-Real, among others. In addition to his many designs for PNB, he has designed for San Francisco Ballet, New York City Ballet, Ballet West , Pennsylvania Ballet, Les Ballets de Monte-Carlo, Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre, Oregon Ballet Theatre, Spectrum Dance Theatre, Peter Boal Solos, and Wear Moi Dancewear of London.
